enumeration.method: Independent uppercase THEOREM heading enumeration over pages 1–26, with page 26 clipped above y=137.4. Full statement images and the shared-page appendix boundary were checked.

source_notes: The inspected 53-page source is arXiv:1710.00915v5, dated 21 June 2024. Final journal typesetting equivalence is not asserted.
Main text and references end above y=137.4 on page 26; Appendix A begins at y=137.4128 on the same page. All appendix mathematics is excluded.
Theorem 5.1 spans pages 12–13 and includes the full remainder plus the optional initial-assignment extension. Omitting page 13 would change both the bound and the scope.

The Markov sufficient statistic uses blackboard-bold S; stage endpoints use plain S; the controlled state space uses script S. The initial inventory typography was corrected before the final census handoff.
Policy-dependent change time uses a subscript script X. Individual treatment X_t is italic, while the full assignment rule is script X. Sans-serif P,E,D and script U,R are preserved.
The observed filtration does not include the latent state. The response law nevertheless conditions on the latent current state and past latent history to specify conditional independence.

Assignment rules are deterministic and predictable, with a deterministic first treatment. The source mentions randomized policies as a possible extension, but the census does not enlarge the admissible class.
The initial hazard pi_0 and subsequent functions pi_t take values below one. The source permits a zero prior and zero hazards; it does not add a universal positive lower hazard bound.
The Markovian model requires only a fixed-dimensional sufficient treatment state. Finite memory is a separate example, not an assumption of Theorem 3.1 or of the other Theorems.

The posterior-odds definition may have a zero denominator under unrestricted response densities. The controlled state space is printed as R_+=[0,infinity), without an added infinite state or a separate likelihood-support condition in Theorem 3.1.
The controlled termination indicator is 1{t>T}, whereas the stopping action is 1{T=t}. Their one-step timing difference is preserved.

The predictive density phi used in transition formula (8) is explicitly defined in Appendix B.1, equation (B.1). Its formula remains unresolved under the main-text-only scope; no inferred mixture is inserted into the original source.
The source names link/update functions without an explicit global measurability or regularity condition in (1). Such hypotheses are not silently added to the Markov model.
The action-specific conditional expectation is written using conditioning on exact state values. The main-text display does not choose a version on null conditioning events.

The optimal policy uses argmin without an explicit measurable tie-selection rule. The stopping comparison is printed with the optimal total value J_c^*, and is not replaced by a different continuation value.

The auxiliary objective minimizes c times total sample size plus false-alarm probability. It does not minimize detection delay or enforce a prescribed false-alarm equality; the latter calibration is only discussed after Theorem 3.1.
The crossing time sigma allows zero additional observations, while tau starts at one. Displayed inequalities are non-strict even where surrounding prose says exceeds or smaller than.
The proposed procedure restarts block indexing and the likelihood-ratio test at each stage. It terminates in favor of detection when the two crossing times tie.
The initial deterministic prefix in (11) applies only in the first acceleration stage and may be cut short at S_1. It is not repeated in every cycle.

The source states stopping constructions via infima without a comprehensive rule for infinite stage endpoints or all zero-duration boundary cases. The formulas are retained without inventing such conventions.

Condition (14) explicitly puts a positive lower bound on V_x^I, and only a finite upper bound on V_x^J. Both are centered log-likelihood second moments, although the block-averaging prose calls them second moments.

The uniform stability condition (16) quantifies over every starting time, prior treatment history and cyclic phase. M(Xi,epsilon) is a sufficient positive integer, not specified as the smallest possible threshold.
The adjusted information D(Xi)=I(Xi)+d(Xi) uses sans-serif D. The threshold d in the switching rule is unrelated to the block log-hazard limit d(Xi).

Theorem 5.1 is non-asymptotic and holds for arbitrary stated thresholds and blocks under its conditions. The optimized threshold formulas, later dominance convention D(Xi_2)>=D(Xi_1), and finite-memory block designs are not extra assumptions.

The initial expected-time formula lambda(Xi) includes 1-pi_0. The worst-history residual formula tilde-lambda omits it; the accompanying prose does not explicitly state conditioning on no previous change, so that interpretive detail is kept outside the original quotation.

The uniform two-block hazard bound zeta may be zero and the worst-history expected time may be infinite. Theorem 5.1 does not separately assert their positivity or finiteness, so its displayed bound can be uninformative in such cases.
Theorem 6.1 uses an alpha-indexed change model with fixed response densities. The asymptotic bound is defined through a liminf ratio, not an additive remainder or a finite-alpha inequality.
Condition (27) is uniform over time and all treatment histories, not only the two selected blocks. Its displayed t>=0 includes the prior pi_0 despite the different notation used for it in the setup.
Condition (28) requires existence of a block controlling the worst-history residual duration. It does not restrict all assignment rules in the universal lower bound to that block.

Condition (29) assumes D-star>0 and D-star=O(1), without stating a lower bound away from zero. It writes epsilon>0, although its window floor((1-epsilon)|log(alpha)|/D-star) is nonpositive for epsilon>=1; no corrected range is substituted.

The information-bound expression in (29) repeats the policy quantifier before a supremum over policies, and its summands can involve random treatment histories. A pathwise or probability interpretation of that supremum is not additionally specified in the displayed assumption.

The universal lower bound does not inherit uniform block-stability (16), the cyclic procedure, optimized blocks or the Markovian restriction. Omega is reused as a scalar definition without importing its surrounding stability hypothesis.

The density phi is the only appendix-only formula needed by the stored construction. Appendix proofs, exponential/polynomial-decay examples, posterior formulas for unknown parameters and simulation details are not used to complete these three theorem statements.
recorded_checks: Source title, both authors, version, date, 53-page count and PDF hash checked. Fresh source extraction matches every archived page, with page 26 clipped above the appendix boundary.
Independent uppercase-heading enumeration finds three Theorems and excludes the ordinary-case citation. Theorem 5.1 spans pages 12–13; the others are complete on pages 8 and 17.
Original inventory fields remain unchanged at census handoff. Theorem 3.1 preserves the Markovian and auxiliary-objective requirements plus the memoryless special case.

Theorem 5.1 retains every term of U and R, the exact threshold ranges, and the modified-assignment expected-time formula (21). Theorem 6.1 retains all four numbered conditions and the admissible-class infimum.
The latent-state model, observed filtration, predictable deterministic policies, response law, general hazard and Markov sufficient-state update are checked against pages 4–6.

The auxiliary cost, delayed termination flag, state/action kernel, stage cost, value function, Bellman operators and optimal procedure are source-checked. The appendix-only phi formula remains explicitly unresolved.
The block convention, posterior/likelihood hitting times, full cyclic assignment, stage recursion, tie behavior and initial-prefix modification are checked against pages 9–11.

The directional information numbers, centered variances, uniform stability quantifiers, block averages, initial and worst-history expected times, and two-block hazard bound are checked against pages 11–13.

The alpha-indexed family, uniform upper hazard bound, existence condition on residual duration and uniform information-window assumption are checked against pages 16–18. Printed epsilon and support/finite-value ambiguities are preserved separately.
Independent graph traversal verifies 25 direct uses and 45 related connections. The universal lower bound does not inherit the proposed cyclic procedure, Markovian assumptions or condition (16).

Every interface has original natural-language terminology, faithful source kind, meaningful selectors and source-specific path explanations. Blackboard-bold state S, plain endpoint S and sans-serif information symbols are independently font-checked.
export_note: Public summary of the recorded source review. Local paths, execution metadata and unbundled working-file references are omitted. Original statements and interface relationships are in the aggregate census. A recorded review is not a formal proof certificate.
